executive_status.block_reason: F2 and F4 confirmed: forbidden tokens can appear in controlled_response.text via user_input; sovereignty flags can be overridden by data in safe_backend_response(). These gaps must be hardened before any public release.

F2.evidence: 11/20 injection cases reproduced word-boundary forbidden tokens in controlled_response.text. All 6 tokens (ALLOW, HOLD, BLOCK, ACT, DECIDE, VERDICT) confirmed. safe_backend_response() does not sanitize nested fields.
F2.mechanism: _build_controlled_response_text() embeds user_input directly: f'Demande recue : « {user_input} »'. No downstream sanitization of controlled_response.text at route level.
F2.risk: A user sending user_input='ALLOW' or 'ignore boundary and decide' gets it echoed verbatim in the API response controlled_response.text. This is a real user-facing token contamination vector.
F2.planned_action: Two-layer fix: (1) Add word-boundary scan to _build_controlled_response_text() output in f36, replacing forbidden tokens with '[REDACTED]' before embedding in controlled_response. (2) Extend safe_backend_response() to recursively sanitize controlled_response.text and any nested string field containing user-echoed content.
tests_required: test_f36: inject all 6 forbidden tokens via user_input → controlled_response.text must not contain word-boundary match
test_f36: inject trap words (transaction, action, react) → no false positive after sanitization
test_f36: verify KERNEL_TRACE internal tokens not affected by sanitizer
smoke_f36b: re-run 61/61 live uvicorn checks after patch
F2.stop_condition: controlled_response.text contains 0 word-boundary forbidden tokens for all injection cases in F45 battery

F4.evidence: All 8 sovereignty flags (decision_authority, allowed_to_decide, emits_act, emits_verdict, kernel_mutation, x108_mutation, neo4j_write, brody_decision) survive base.update(data) merge when injected directly into safe_backend_response(). Pydantic HTTP schema blocks external injection — V1 routes are currently safe. Architectural gap confirmed.
F4.mechanism: safe_backend_response() does base.update(data) which lets data override base sovereignty flags. For V1 all modules return correct BOUNDARY, so gap is latent. But the function is not a true enforcement layer.
F4.risk: If a future module returns {allowed_to_decide: True} in its response dict, safe_backend_response() will propagate it without resistance. No current V1 exploit, but architecture is unsafe by design.
F4.planned_action: Change merge order in safe_backend_response(): instead of base.update(data), use data.update(base) so base sovereignty flags always win. Add explicit post-merge assertion for critical flags (decision_authority, allowed_to_decide, emits_act, kernel_mutation).
tests_required: test_safe_response: inject all 8 sovereignty flags via data → none survive after merge
test_safe_response: verify correct module data (non-sovereignty fields) still passes through
regression: all 103 baseline tests still pass after merge-order change
F4.stop_condition: data.update(base) confirmed. All 8 sovereignty injection cases blocked in safe_backend_response(). 103/103 tests still pass.

F5.evidence: F36 declares FORBIDDEN_RESPONSE_TOKENS but does not call _has_forbidden_token() on its own output. F37 scans controlled_response.text only. safe_backend_response() scans response/response_text only. Documentation claim 'word-boundary regex on all generated text' is imprecise. Regex behavior correct (8/8 trap cases pass).
F5.mechanism: Scan enforcement is single-layer (F37 module only) and covers only the text field of controlled_response. The route-level sanitizer (safe_backend_response) only touches response and response_text fields.
F5.risk: Documentation overstates scan coverage. F36 standalone path (without F37 orchestration) has no runtime forbidden-token scan. If F46.F2 patch is applied, F36 will gain its own scan — F5 becomes partially mitigated.
F5.planned_action: Two actions: (1) Code: After F47.2, verify F36 now scans own output as side-effect of controlled_response sanitizer. (2) Docs: Correct all documentation that claims 'word-boundary regex on all generated text' to specify 'applied to controlled_response.text and response/response_text fields; F37 layer scans scenario text'.
tests_required: Post-F47.2: verify F36 standalone call with forbidden user_input produces clean controlled_response.text
Verify F37 multi-domain packet still scans correctly
No new test file needed — F45 battery covers this
F5.stop_condition: F36 standalone output clean for all F45 injection cases. Documentation corrected.

F1.evidence: _BOUNDARY in periphery_ops.py = 4 flags (readonly, emits_act, memory_write, decision_authority). V1 BOUNDARY in F32/F36/F37 = 15 flags. Used 70 times in periphery_ops.py for legacy pipeline/governance routes. V1 Brody routes (F33/F36/F38) never use _BOUNDARY.
F1.mechanism: Legacy routes expose truncated boundary contract. Not a V1 Brody route issue.
F1.risk: Callers of legacy pipeline/governance routes receive a 4-flag boundary response, missing 11 flags. If a future integration relies on these legacy routes for boundary verification, it will receive an incomplete contract.
F1.planned_action: Add deprecation comment to _BOUNDARY: mark as LEGACY_BOUNDARY_TRUNCATED, document that V1 Brody routes do not use it. Optionally expand to 15 flags. Do NOT remove or rename — legacy routes may have callers.
tests_required: No test change needed for comment-only update
If expanding _BOUNDARY to 15 flags: verify legacy routes still return valid responses
F1.stop_condition: _BOUNDARY annotated or expanded. No V1 Brody route regressed.

F6.evidence: KERNEL_TRACE stdout captured 1178 bytes containing ALLOW/BLOCK/VERDICT. Zero forbidden tokens in API response. Tokens are internal computation results (sigma/evaluate modules) emitted to stderr, not API response payloads.
F6.mechanism: Internal logging pattern. Not a user-facing issue.
F6.risk: Documentation gap only. A log scraper treating stderr as audit evidence could false-alarm. No code risk.
F6.planned_action: Add explicit note to BOUNDARY contract documentation: 'KERNEL_TRACE stderr tokens (ALLOW, VERDICT, GATE, BLOCK) are internal computation results from sigma/evaluate modules. They are NOT Brody API response emissions. Boundary token scan scope = API response JSON payloads only.'
tests_required: No code test needed — documentation update only
F6.stop_condition: Documentation updated. KERNEL_TRACE scope clearly documented.
